claims.text: Rapid thermal annealing at approximately 700°C for seconds to minutes will refine the deposited Cr coating into a uniform ultra-fine-grained microstructure.
The rapid thermal anneal will reduce the density of high-angle grain boundaries in the Cr coating.
High-angle grain boundaries in Cr are fast diffusion paths.
Reducing high-angle grain-boundary density will limit fast diffusion of Cr into the Zr-alloy substrate.
Elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion is responsible for premature failure of the Cr coating.
The RTP treatment will significantly suppress elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The RTP-modified coating will exhibit less Cr–Zr interdiffusion than the untreated coarse-grained coating.
The RTP-modified coating will retain its integrity longer than the untreated baseline.
The RTP-modified coating will improve performance during exposure to approximately 320°C water.
The RTP-modified coating will improve performance during transient exposure to steam near 1200°C.
Conventional elemental Cr coatings produced by typical physical vapor deposition have a coarse-grained structure.
The proposed microstructure can remain beneficial without compromising adhesion during repeated thermal cycles.
